corpus: SkyEye demo corpus — drone-altitude imagery only
notes: Every image is a public, openly licensed drone/aerial photograph taken at drone altitude (nadir or near-nadir). No satellite tiles, no live surveillance, no private footage.

Purpose-built SAR datasets (HERIDAL, SARD, C2A) are access-gated behind request forms or Kaggle auth, so this corpus stands in for them: openly licensed nadir drone photos where humans occupy only a few dozen pixels — the same detection difficulty.
Image blobs are gitignored. Run 'python fixtures/fetch_fixtures.py' from backend/ to download them.
expected_min_detections is a human-eyeballed floor used by the smoke test, not ground-truth annotation.

samples.label: Single person lying on a lawn (nadir)
samples.why_included: Closest analogue to a real SAR subject: one immobile person, prone, viewed straight down against open ground.

samples.label: Lone surfer in breaking surf (nadir)
samples.source: Wikimedia Commons — "La Jolla, CA San Diego Surfer on Beach Aerial View"
samples.commons_title: File:La Jolla, CA San Diego Surfer on Beach Aerial View.jpg
samples.attribution: See the Commons file page for the required author credit
samples.why_included: Single subject against a high-clutter background — tests false-positive behaviour on foam texture.
samples.known_miss: Pretrained YOLOv8n does not detect this subject at any threshold (0.06 confidence at conf=0.05). It is a pose failure, not a scale failure: a person lying prone on a board seen from directly above does not match COCO's upright-person prior, and tiling cannot fix it. Kept in the corpus deliberately as an honest failure case.

samples.label: Scattered people among palm shadows (nadir)
samples.why_included: Dozens of small, well-separated people plus palm shadows that mimic human shapes.

samples.label: Busy beachfront, very small subjects (nadir)
samples.why_included: Hardest case: people are only a few pixels tall, next to umbrellas and vehicles that invite false positives. This is where tiling earns its place.

samples.label: Swimmers in shallow surf (nadir)
samples.why_included: Partially occluded bodies in water — the water-search analogue of a subject under partial cover.

samples.label: Surfers spread across a bay (nadir)
samples.source: Wikimedia Commons — "Surfing in Vazon Bay, Guernsey (Unsplash)"
samples.why_included: Wide-area sparse search: a handful of tiny subjects spread over a large frame.

samples.label: Conifer stand and bare clearing, no people (nadir)
samples.terrain: conifer canopy, logged ground, scattered debris
samples.why_included: True negative over exactly the terrain a wilderness search flies. Branches and stumps are the classic false-positive trap.

samples.label: Dense wooded valley, no people
samples.source: Wikimedia Commons — "Aerial view of forest canopy and waterfall, Sitakunda Eco Park"
samples.commons_title: File:Aerial view of forest canopy and waterfall, Sitakunda Eco Park⁠.jpg
samples.attribution: See the Commons file page for the required author credit
samples.why_included: Second true negative, and an honest reminder that closed canopy hides a subject from any optical sensor.
